title: Canonical finite-coefficient derived composition is ordinary module composition localized
statement: For any composable scheme morphisms h:Z→W and k:W→V and any finite commutative ring A, the inverse of the canonical derived comparison proEtaleConstantRingPullbackComposition(h,k,A) is the localization of the canonical ordinary module comparison of [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition], followed by the exact-functor derived composition isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both ordinary comparisons use the canonical constant-ring inverse-image identifications [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 0D6D, derived pullback composition on flat-term K-flat representatives; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D8 for the ordinary compositor.

proof.text: The canonical module adjunction has the normalized tensor unit by lem-pod-canonical-module-adjunction-unit. Uniqueness of the normalized adjunction identifies it with the one used in the canonical derived comparison. Both direct-image comparators restrict sections along exactly the same fibre-product isomorphism, so extensionality identifies them. Conjugation is injective, hence the ordinary comparators coincide. Apply the established representative computation of the canonical derived comparison and substitute this equality. No arbitrary data witness is chosen.

theorem proEtaleConstantRingPullbackComposition_eq_mapModuleComparison
    {V W Z : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ W) (k : W ⟶ V)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] :
    (proEtaleConstantRingPullbackComposition h k A).symm =
      Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
        (proEtaleConstantRingModulePullbackComposition h k A).choose ≪≫
      Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
        (proEtaleConstantRingPullback A k) (proEtaleConstantRingPullback A h)
